title: What is code quality, really?
look: Session board: code cards, file tiles and small charts on a dot-grid desk. Plain. Colors and type from the Zen-Sumi design system: washi paper, sumi ink, rationed vermillion, jade for healthy. The Sensei mark on the close.

scenes.name: Really?
scenes.desc: What is code quality, really? Elegant, clever, short: the usual answers are crossed out.

scenes.name: Easy to change
scenes.desc: Quality is how cheaply and safely the next change can be made: read, find, change once, know nothing broke.

scenes.name: Four signals
scenes.desc: Duplication, complexity smells, coverage and churn: four signals you can measure.

scenes.name: The trend
scenes.desc: 8% and falling beats 4% and climbing: read the direction, not the number.

scenes.name: Real history
scenes.desc: Sensei measures sampled commits across your git history: qlty, your test runs, git.

scenes.name: Sensei
scenes.desc: End card with the Sensei mark: quality is a trajectory.
